title: Open Your First Feature Branch and Pull Request
objective: Create a feature branch, commit a small real change with clear messages, and open a pull request with a description a reviewer could act on.
whyThisMatters: Almost every professional change to a shared codebase goes through the same loop: branch, commit, push, open a pull request. Doing it once slowly and deliberately, before doing it under real deadline pressure, is the point of this task.
evidence: A link to the actual pull request
The branch's commit log (via git log output or the PR's commits tab)
AI disclosure entry if AI helped write commit messages or the PR description
acceptanceCriteria: The branch name follows a consistent, documented convention (for example feature/<short-description>) that you can explain.
The branch contains at least two commits, each with a message describing what changed and why, not just 'wip' or 'fix'.
A pull request exists comparing the branch to the base branch, with a description stating what changed, why, and how to verify it.
The PR is linked in the submission and remains viewable by the mentor.
